newsitem.title: UK: Ldn freight - Rates said to soften in US Gulf.
newsitem.headline: Ldn freight - Rates said to soften in US Gulf.

text.p: Further evidence of softening rate levels in the US Gulf caused the BFI to lose 11 points to 1504.

New cargoes have been slow to materialize in the Mississippi with congestion now said to be running at about 10 days and causing charterers to face big demurrage bills for fresh orders. Elsewhere Panamax rates appeared largely unchanged, possibly a little firmer from the Continent. The S American market still lacks strength but there are few signs of weakness in the Middle East and Far East. Brokers reported sales for scrap of the 1974-built Forum Trader 64,000 dwt to Indian buyers at $170 per ldwt and Forest Prince 41,901 dwt at $174 to Bangladesh. These rates were thought to be only marginally better than last month in a generally sluggish market.

The fixture of Sun P 65,000 dwt by IrisL delivery prompt Le Havre trip Iran at $13,500 daily was a fair indication of the relative state of demand on different sides of the North Atlantic. Brokers reported a number of Panamax units available for November loading in the US Gulf although outstanding orders for prompt vessels, such as Dreyfus US Gulf/Continent and Continental US Gulf/Turkey, remain to be covered.

It was rumoured that Goldbeam had booked 52-54,000 heavy grain US Gulf/Japan for early Dec at between $24.10 and 24.25 basis no combo, a further decline from rates agreed in the middle of last week in the region of $25.00/25.25.

MSK were reported from Tokyo to have fixed Andre tonnage for similar business for first quarter 1997 at only $22.75 no combo. Cargill confirmed their fixture of Ispat Guarav 71,535 dwt delivery Santos Nov/Dec for 2 laden legs Atlantic business redelivery Continent at $11,750 daily plus $175,000 bonus and these charterers quoted a fresh enquiry this morning for a Panamax for up river and Brazil/Continent grain for early Dec loading.

Firmer Panamax rates were seen in the Pacific with reports of 54,000 heavy grain fixed NoPac/Taiwan at $16.60 and the same quantity NoPac/Japan at $16.25 no combo, both for early Dec. Handy-size business included reports of Andre covering a prompt stem of 21,000 wheat Rouen/Morocco at $12.25 and Bunge 25,000/5 wheat Vancouverr/1-3 ports Brazil at $26.00.

Several Capers have fixed and failed on subjects, China Prosperity 151,013 dwt in the Atlantic, for example, United Resolve 150,149 dwt in the Far East, and Mount Athos for 130,000/10 ironore Saldanha/Beilun for Dec 15/30 with Great Chance at $8.95.

Mineral Europe 170,000 dwt was believed fixed by Yukong from Port Talbot via Brazil to S Korea, Jean L D 165,000 dwt for a transAtlantic round on subjects, and Navalis 133,000 dwt from China mid Dec to S Korean charterers, but full details were lacking. British Steel were understood to have taken Nord-Energy 151,000 dwt last week for ironore from Cape Lambert to UK on private terms.

Rates for Panamaxes in the mineral trades continued reasonably steady in the Far East. NYK booked a couple of modern types delivery prompt Far East for Australian rounds at between $12,750 and $13,000 daily. Cetragpa fixed the Van Ommeren-relet Evgenia 69,000 dwt delivery prompt Ulsan for a coal trip via Roberts Bank to Lisbon at $8,250 daily. Showa failed on subjects with the 1983-built Kavo Kalliakra 64,861 dwt delivery Kosichang for a trip via Goa to Japan at about $10,500 daily, said to be on account of the vessel's length. The 1977-built Astor 64,833 dwt was taken with mid-Dec delivery by GIC for limestone from U.A.E. to Hongkong at a steady $10,800 daily.

Brokers reported quiet conditions throughout the Atlantic, but better enquiry in the Far East. Hanjin were said to have fixed a 37,500 dwt craned bulker in the Pacific for 2-4 months and Korea Line were rumoured to have fixed Georgi 38,000 dwt for a NoPac round at a firm $7,500 daily, brokers reported.
